title: Cannot map / key to END
summary: The physical slash key on an ASUS ProArt StudioBook remains slash after being captured for remapping to End. A neighboring asterisk-to-Home remap works.
next_action: Compare the key identity captured by Settings with what Keyboard Manager sees during normal typing, using the working neighbor and a standard numpad as controls.

judgment.rationale: The reporter corrected the affected key and confirmed physical capture rather than selection from the list. The report does not yet identify the failing key path.
judgment.recommended_action: Compare slash-versus-Divide identity and remap behavior; do not ask again whether physical capture was used.

fix_assessment.rationale: No evidence shows whether the key identity differs between capture and runtime or whether a correctly identified key fails later in remapping.

actions.label: Compare captured and runtime identities for the slash key

reproduce.title: Isolate the keyboard-specific slash-to-End remap
reproduce.version_requirement: PowerToys 0.102.3101.0; compare with the current stable build
prerequisites: Affected ASUS keyboard or comparable model, plus a standard keyboard with separate slash and numpad Divide keys.
setup: Use a disposable mapping profile and a plain-text editor with a nonempty line to distinguish End from typed slash.
steps: Capture the affected physical key in the remap editor, set it to End, save, and press it in the text editor.
Record the source key identity during capture and normal typing. Compare with main-keyboard slash, numpad Divide and the working asterisk-to-Home control.
If capture and runtime identities match but output differs, locate the first stage where the expected End mapping is lost.
reproduce.expected_result: The captured physical key moves the caret to the line end without inserting slash. A failed test distinguishes mismatched identity from failed remap dispatch.

issue_context.summary: Physical key capture succeeds, but slash-to-End fails on the reporter's laptop.
known_information: The reporter clarified that slash, not asterisk, is affected and that the key was physically pressed in the capture dialog.
inferences: An OEM key or numpad translation difference is plausible but not demonstrated.
issue_context.analysis: Compare the key presented to the capture and remapping paths before changing mapping behavior. The adjacent working key is a control for general remapper availability.
initial_investigation: Read the original report and correction thread; no hardware reproduction was performed.
information_gaps: The source key identity in each path and whether the same behavior occurs on a standard numpad are not known.

status.label: Needs Maintainer Verification
status.detail: Verify the captured and runtime IDs of the affected key before proposing a fix.
